decision: which pre-row job opens a legacy first row's visit
choice: the newest attempt-1 job of the row's state after the oldest such job; attempt-2 jobs stay with their first attempt
why: queue time cannot tell a T6 retry (attempt 2) from a fresh enqueue: a retry 1 s before a script-only row and a review queued 1000 s before a late label write both broke the 60 s cutoff (PR #376 r1 f-2)

choice: jobs.attempt, read by lib/dashboard.py into JobStep.attempt (default 1)
why: the column is NOT NULL in every jobs table, and T6 and orch retry both queue attempt 2

decision: which legacy first rows may claim a pre-row job at all
choice: only a set-state row; any other writer's row (ship-discard, update-settled, ...) opens a script visit and leaves every pre-row job to the older visits
why: set-state is the one writer that queues the new state's job before writing the row (polls earlier when the label write fails); attempt numbers alone gave a completed attempt-1 review at 1144 to a ship-discard row at 1244 (PR #376 r2 f-2). The row's source is already recorded, so the dashboard reads it instead of guessing
